Subject lines

  • Subject lineYour [QUOTE OR PROPOSAL] for [PROJECT]
  • Subject lineNext steps from our call on [DATE]
  • Subject lineYour question about [PRODUCT OR SERVICE]

Why this works

  1. Start with the thing you are following up on, and its date.
  2. Ask one question. A reply of one line should be enough.
  3. Say what happens next, and who does it.
  4. Use the person's own words from the call or the form, not yours.
  5. Write down the date you will follow up again.

What to avoid

  • Do not ask "any updates?". Ask about one specific thing: the price, the scope, the date.
  • Do not push them to decide. Ask what they need in order to decide.
  • Do not mention a competitor or a price rise to hurry them, unless it is true and they asked.
  • Do not send three different asks in one email.

Official pages. Rules for commercial email differ by country. Not legal advice: check the rules that apply to you.

  • United States: FTC: CAN-SPAM Act: A Compliance Guide for Business. It says the law covers all commercial email, with no exception for business-to-business email, and lists what each message needs, read 5 October 2026.
  • United Kingdom: ICO: Electronic mail marketing. It says you must not send marketing emails to individuals without specific consent, that you can send marketing emails to companies, and that it is good practice to keep a do-not-email list of companies that object. The ICO says the page is under review. Read 5 October 2026.

See what it does

What should a sales follow-up email say?

Name the thing you are following up on, such as the quote, the call or the trial. Add one useful fact and ask one question. Make the next step clear and easy to say yes or no to.

How soon should I follow up after a quote?

Within a few working days is common, while the quote is fresh. If you hear nothing, follow up again about a week later with something new, not the same words.

Should I attach something to a follow-up?

Only if it answers a question they asked. Extra attachments make the email harder to answer.

What if they went quiet after a quote?

Ask one simple question, such as whether the timing has changed. A yes or no is easy to answer.

Questions people ask

When should I follow up after sending a proposal?

Pick a date at the end of the call, such as "I will check in on Thursday", and do it. Agreeing the date in advance makes the follow-up expected.

What should a sales follow-up email say?

What you are following up on, one question, and the next step. Anything else can wait for a call.

What if they said they need to think about it?

Ask what they need in order to decide, and offer it: a number, a reference, a call with someone. Then leave them to it.

Is a follow-up a marketing email?

It can be. The rules depend on the country and on who you write to. See the pointers on this page, and check them for your case.
